questions.scenario: The product team adds a new payment method, `Ussd`, to the sealed interface `PaymentMethod`. You want the build to fail everywhere fees, limits and receipts don't yet handle it.
questions.question: How must those switches be written for that to happen?
options: As if/else chains with instanceof
With a case null branch
As switch expressions over PaymentMethod with one case per permitted type and no default branch
With a default branch that throws UnsupportedOperationException
questions.explanation: Exhaustiveness checking over a sealed hierarchy only works when you don't add default. With default, the new type falls into it silently and the failure moves to runtime.

questions.scenario: `record Statement(String account, List<Transaction> lines) {}` is created from a caller's ArrayList. Later the caller clears its list and the statement becomes empty.
questions.question: What should the record do?
options: Nothing; records are deeply immutable
Copy defensively in a compact constructor: lines = List.copyOf(lines);
Declare lines as final
Override equals
questions.explanation: Records are shallowly immutable: the field can't be reassigned, but the list it points to can change. List.copyOf takes an unmodifiable snapshot (and rejects nulls).

questions.scenario: This switch fails to compile: `case Card c -> standardFee(c); case Card c when c.international() -> fxFee(c);`
questions.question: Why?
options: International cards need a default branch
Guards are not allowed on records
You can't have two cases for the same type
The unguarded Card case dominates the guarded one, so the second case can never match; put the guarded case first
questions.explanation: Cases are tested top to bottom. Any Card matches the first case, so the compiler rejects the unreachable, more specific case. Order specific (guarded) cases before general ones.

questions.scenario: A junior developer annotates a record `CustomerEntity` with `@Entity` to use it with JPA, and Hibernate fails at startup.
questions.question: What's the best guidance?
options: Make the record non-sealed
Records are a good fit for DTOs and value objects, but JPA entities need a no-arg constructor and mutable state, so keep entities as regular classes
Add setters to the record
Use @Embeddable on every component
questions.explanation: Records have final fields and only a canonical constructor, which conflicts with how JPA providers create and update entities. Use records for request/response DTOs, events and value objects.

questions.scenario: You need to pull the bank code and account number out of a `BankTransfer(String bankCode, String accountNumber)` inside an if statement, in one step.
questions.question: Which Java 21 syntax does that?
options: if (m instanceof BankTransfer) { var b = (BankTransfer) m; }
if (m instanceof BankTransfer.class) { ... }
if (m instanceof BankTransfer(String bank, String acct)) { ... }
if (m.equals(BankTransfer)) { ... }
questions.explanation: A record pattern tests the type and deconstructs the components into new variables in one expression. The cast-based version works but is the pre-Java-16 style.

questions.scenario: A text block SQL query has unwanted leading spaces on every line in the log, because the closing `"""` is on its own line, indented further right than the SQL.
questions.question: How is indentation in a text block determined?
options: It is always kept exactly as typed
Incidental indentation is stripped up to the least-indented line, and the closing delimiter's line counts
Only tabs are removed
All leading whitespace is removed
questions.explanation: The compiler removes the common leading whitespace across all lines, including the closing delimiter's line. Moving the closing quotes left or right changes how much is kept.

questions.scenario: You are choosing where to use records in a new transfer service.
questions.question: Which are good fits for records?
options: A `TransferCompleted` event published after posting
A JPA `@Entity` for the account table with lazy-loaded relationships
A `TransferRequest` JSON request body
A `Money(BigDecimal amount, Currency currency)` value object
questions.explanation: Request DTOs, value objects and events are immutable data carriers, exactly what records model. JPA entities need mutability and proxies.

questions.scenario: A JPA entity uses Lombok's `@Data`. Adding entities to a `HashSet` and then saving them makes the set behave strangely, and logs show a customer's BVN.
questions.question: What is the problem?
options: Lombok doesn't support HashSet
@Data generates equals/hashCode over all fields (including the generated id) and a toString that prints every field, including sensitive ones
The BVN field must be static
JPA entities can't have getters
questions.explanation: Use explicit equals/hashCode for entities and exclude sensitive fields from toString, or avoid @Data on entities.
